summary: Christoph Kleine works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD and completed his Habilitation at the University of Marburg, held a postdoctoral post at EFEO, and was a professor at LMU Munich before joining Leipzig University.

Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held the Chair of Asian Anthropology at the University of London from circa 1951 to 1976 and was attested as a professor at SOAS in 1988.
Christophe Vielle is an Indologist who taught Sandra Smets. He served as professeur de sanskrit at KU Leuven (attested 2009) and as a professor at Université catholique de Louvain (attested 2013).

Christopher André Holmboe was a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Oslo and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval, later serving as reader and professor at Oslo.

Christopher Byrne specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from McGill University, studying under doctoral supervisor Grace S. Fong, MA supervisor G. Victor Sōgen Hori, and teacher Robin D. S. Yates.
Christopher D. Emms is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his studies at McMaster University under the doctoral supervision of Shayne Clarke.

Christopher D. Wallis works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Rochester, the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, and UC Berkeley under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt. He lectured at Naropa University in 2020.

Christopher Framarin specializes in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaii and a PhD at the University of New Mexico, later becoming an associate professor at the University of Calgary.

Christopher Hatchell is a Tibetologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under the mentorship of David Germano and committee members Paul Groner, Karen C. Lang, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Robert A. Hueckstedt.

Christopher I. Beckwith is a linguist and scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Ohio State and Indiana University under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu, later holding academic appointments at Indiana University.

Christopher Ives is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He was an assistant professor of religion at the University of Puget Sound from circa 1987 to 2001 and became professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College circa 2001.

Christopher Jon Jensen works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan, Kyoto University, and McMaster University (PhD), supervised by James A. Benn and taught by Tōru Funayama, Shayne Clarke, Mark Rowe, and Noel Salmond.

Christopher Kelley is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who founded the Columbia Society for Comparative Philosophy. After earning his PhD at Columbia University, he taught there, at The New School, and at Brooklyn College.

Christopher Key Chapple works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He held positions at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions, Stony Brook University, and Loyola Marymount University, where he was named Doshi Professor of Indic and Comparative Theology.

Christopher Minkowski is an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Harvard. He held positions at Brown University, the University of Iowa, Cornell University (circa 1989–2005), and served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford and Balliol College (circa 2005–2023).

Christopher Pinney is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts at the Australian National University from circa 1996 to 1999 and at University College London beginning circa 1999.

Christopher S. George, founder of the American Institute of Buddhist Studies, works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Columbia under Royal W. Weiler, learned from Padma Gyaltsen and Geshe Wangyal, and became a professor at IASWR.

Christopher S. Queen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. At Harvard University, he served as Dean of Students for Continuing Education and lecturer on the Study of Religion (circa 1989) and Lecturer on Buddhism and World Religions (circa 1990).

Chu-tsing Li was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Iowa from circa 1948 to 1955 and later held a post at the University of Kansas from circa 1966 to 1990.

Chuan-ying Yen specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University, where she studied under doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield, tutor Chu-tsing Li, and teacher John Hay.
